title: The pond that fills overnight
hook: Algae doubles daily and fills the pond on day 30. How full was it on day 25?

knows: percentages and fractions such as one half and one quarter
doesNotKnow: exponents or powers of 2 as notation

misconception: Growth is roughly proportional to elapsed time: five sixths of the way to the deadline means about five sixths of the way to full.
objective: The learner can explain why, under steady doubling, the pond is half full only one day before it is full and about 3% full five days before, so most of the visible change happens at the very end.

claims.text: If the covered area doubles every day and the pond is full on day 30, the coverage on day d is (1/2)^(30 - d) of the pond.
claims.source: Run the doubling backwards: each day earlier halves the coverage. Standard exponential model, e.g. Stewart, Calculus, sec. 3.8 (Exponential Growth and Decay).

claims.text: On day 29 the pond is half covered and on day 28 a quarter, so three quarters of the pond fills in the last two days; on day 25 it is 1/32 covered, about 3%.
On day 20 the algae covers about one thousandth of the pond (1/1024).
Doubling 30 times multiplies a quantity by more than a billion.
The pond puzzle is a classic illustration of exponential growth; a version appears in the 1972 report The Limits to Growth.
claims.source: Meadows, Meadows, Randers and Behrens, The Limits to Growth (Universe Books, 1972), ch. 1, the lily pond riddle.

claims.text: The pond picture is a 32 x 32 grid of 1,024 equal squares, so each small square is 1/1024 of the pond, and on day 20 the algae covers exactly one such square.
claims.source: Demo.tsx GRID = 32, 32 x 32 = 1024; c1 gives (1/2)^10 = 1/1024 for day 20.

claims.text: A pond that looks 97% clear (3% covered, as on day 25) is five days from full.
claims.source: Day 25 coverage is 1/32 (c2), so 1 - 1/32 = 96.875%, rounded to 97%; 30 - 25 = 5 days.

claims.text: Guessing 'proportional to the days' gives about 83% for day 25 (25 of 30 days).
If a town's cases double every 3 days and the hospital is full in 12 days, today it is 1/16 full (about 6%).

recall.question: A town's number of cases doubles every 3 days. The hospital will be full in 12 days. How full is it today?
recall.why: 12 days is 4 doublings, so today is 1/2 x 1/2 x 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/16 of full. Doubling looks small until the last few steps.
